correctness.rationale: The exact outermost-symbol partition is a bijective enumeration of nonempty distinct palindrome patterns. When both binary symbols repeat, same-endpoint and opposite-endpoint cases bound by 4+M(n-2)+M(n-4) and 4+2M(n-3); singleton/constant cases are strict for n>=4. Fibonacci identities (including strict odd-length difference F(m-1)) prove the all-length upper bound. Alternating words and even-length centrally doubled alternating palindromes attain it by the same exact decomposition. Equality forces positions and shorter extremizers inductively, giving all and only the stated maximizers. The package contains a separate interval-DP checker, direct brute-subsequence enumeration and finite classification verification; these corroborate but do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2021 primary text states the same general observable, tabulates fixed binary counts only through length ten, proves its q-dependent capacity formula under q>=n/2, and explicitly leaves q<n/2 open. Initial small values are not claimed new; residual risk of a missed equivalent formulation is recorded.

value.rationale: The 2021 primary paper explicitly identifies the tight fixed-alphabet regime q<n/2 as outstanding; the binary q=2 case is fundamental. This all-length exact Fibonacci capacity and complete maximizing-word classification supplies a theorem rather than an isolated enumeration or a generic dynamic-programming exercise. The decomposition and parity-sensitive equality classification also give structural information useful for future low-alphabet extremal questions; no larger alphabet result is asserted.
